source.text: בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם אֵ֥ין מֶ֖לֶךְ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וּבַיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֗ם שֵׁ֣בֶט הַדָּנִ֞י מְבַקֶּשׁ־ל֤וֹ נַֽחֲלָה֙ לָשֶׁ֔בֶת כִּי֩ לֹֽא־נָ֨פְלָה לּ֜וֹ עַד־הַיּ֥וֹם הַה֛וּא בְּתוֹךְ־שִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּנַחֲלָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: In the days the those [there was] no king in Israel; and in the days the those the tribe of the Danite[s] [was] seeking for itself an inheritance to dwell [in], for not had fallen to it until the day the that in [the] midst of [the] tribes of Israel in inheritance.

en.L: In those days [there was] no king in Israel. And in those days the tribe of the Danites was seeking for itself an inheritance to live in, for until that day [none] had fallen to it among the tribes of Israel as an inheritance.
en.B: In those days there was no king in Israel. In those days, too, the tribe of Dan was looking for territory of its own to settle in, because until then no inheritance had fallen to it among the tribes of Israel.
en.R: At that time Israel had no king. And at that time the tribe of Dan was looking for land of its own where its people could settle. Until then they had not received their share of land among the tribes of Israel.

sw.L: Katika siku hizo hapakuwa na mfalme katika Israeli. Na katika siku hizo kabila la Wadani lilikuwa likijitafutia urithi wa kukaa, kwa maana mpaka siku hiyo [urithi] ulikuwa haujawaangukia katikati ya makabila ya Israeli.
sw.B: Siku hizo hapakuwa na mfalme katika Israeli. Siku hizo pia kabila la Dani lilikuwa likitafuta eneo lake lenyewe la kukaa, kwa sababu mpaka wakati huo halikuwa limeangukiwa na urithi kati ya makabila ya Israeli.
sw.R: Wakati huo Israeli hawakuwa na mfalme. Na wakati huo kabila la Dani lilikuwa likitafuta nchi yake lenyewe ambapo watu wake wangeweza kukaa. Mpaka wakati huo walikuwa hawajapata sehemu yao ya nchi kati ya makabila ya Israeli.

decisions.choice: in those days there was no king in Israel: the refrain that frames the last chapters of the book
decisions.reason: The same words open the stories of Micah's shrine (17:6), of the Levite and his concubine (19:1), and close the book (21:25), where they are joined to "each did what was right in his own eyes." Here the short form stands alone. The refrain tells the reader that what follows happened in a time without a king to keep order, and it invites the reader to judge what the Danites do.

decisions.choice: had not fallen to it: Dan had not come into a settled share of land
decisions.reason: Land was divided among the tribes by lot, and a share is said to "fall" to a tribe (Numbers 34:2; Joshua 23:4). Dan had been given its towns by lot (Joshua 19:40-46), but the Amorites pressed the Danites back into the hills and would not let them come down into the plain (Judges 1:34). So the sentence does not mean that Dan was left out of the division, but that it had never come to hold a share of its own to live in. Joshua 19:47 tells briefly of the move that this chapter tells at length.

decisions.choice: inheritance: land held by a tribe or family as its lasting share
decisions.reason: The word names land handed down within a family or tribe, received as a gift and not to be sold away (Numbers 27:7; 36:7). The Danites are looking not just for a place to stay but for a home that would be theirs for good.

decisions.choice: the tribe of Dan; territory, land of its own; share of land
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "the tribe of the Danites" and "inheritance" as the Hebrew has them. Balanced says "the tribe of Dan" and "territory of its own" for the first mention of the inheritance, keeping "inheritance" in the second, and Readable speaks of land and a share, which says what the inheritance was.

decisions.choice: "urithi" for the inheritance (L, B); Readable "sehemu yao ya nchi" (their share of land)
decisions.reason: As agreed for these books in every language: "urithi" is land held as a lasting share; Readable says what it was, as the English Readable does.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלְח֣וּ בְנֵי־דָ֣ן׀מִֽמִּשְׁפַּחְתָּ֡ם חֲמִשָּׁ֣ה אֲנָשִׁ֣ים מִקְצוֹתָם֩ אֲנָשִׁ֨ים בְּנֵי־חַ֜יִל מִצָּרְעָ֣ה וּמֵֽאֶשְׁתָּאֹ֗ל לְרַגֵּ֤ל אֶת־הָאָ֨רֶץ֙ וּלְחָקְרָ֔הּ וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֲלֵהֶ֔ם לְכ֖וּ חִקְר֣וּ אֶת־הָאָ֑רֶץ וַיָּבֹ֤אוּ הַר־אֶפְרַ֨יִם֙ עַד־בֵּ֣ית מִיכָ֔ה וַיָּלִ֖ינוּ שָֽׁם׃

records.literal_gloss: And sent [the] sons of Dan from their clan five men from their ends, men, sons of strength, from Zorah and from Eshtaol, to spy out the land and to explore it; and they said to them, Go, explore the land. And they came [to the] hill country of Ephraim, to [the] house of Micah, and they lodged there.

en.L: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Dan sent from their clan five men from their whole number, men of valor, from Zorah and from Eshtaol, to spy out the land and to explore it. And they said to them, "Go, explore the land." And they came to the hill country of Ephraim, to the house of Micah, and they spent the night there.
en.B: So the Danites sent five capable men from their clan, chosen from their whole number, from Zorah and Eshtaol, to spy out and explore the land. They told them, "Go and explore the land." The men came into the hill country of Ephraim as far as Micah's house, and they stayed the night there.
en.R: So the people of Dan chose five brave men from their whole clan. The men came from the towns of Zorah and Eshtaol. The Danites sent them out to spy on the land and explore it. "Go and explore the land," they said to them. The five men went into the hills of Ephraim. They came to Micah's house and spent the night there.

sw.L: Nao wana wa Dani wakatuma kutoka ukoo wao watu watano kutoka katika jumla yao, watu mashujaa, kutoka Sora na kutoka Eshtaoli, ili kuipeleleza nchi na kuichunguza. Wakawaambia, "Nendeni, mkaichunguze nchi." Nao wakafika katika nchi ya milima ya Efraimu, kwenye nyumba ya Mika, wakalala huko.
sw.B: Basi Wadani walituma watu watano hodari kutoka ukoo wao, waliochaguliwa kutoka kwa wote, kutoka Sora na Eshtaoli, ili kuipeleleza nchi na kuichunguza. Wakawaambia, "Nendeni mkaichunguze nchi." Watu hao walifika katika nchi ya milima ya Efraimu mpaka kwenye nyumba ya Mika, wakalala huko.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo watu wa Dani walichagua watu watano jasiri kutoka katika ukoo wao wote. Watu hao walitoka katika miji ya Sora na Eshtaoli. Wadani waliwatuma wakaichunguze nchi na kuipeleleza. Waliwaambia, "Nendeni mkaichunguze nchi." Wale watu watano walikwenda katika milima ya Efraimu. Walifika kwenye nyumba ya Mika, wakalala huko.

decisions.choice: their clan: here the whole tribe of Dan
decisions.reason: Dan is counted as a single clan in the census (Numbers 26:42), so "clan" and "tribe" can name the same group (13:2; 18:11, 19). The men are sent on behalf of all the Danites.

decisions.choice: from their ends: chosen from their whole number
decisions.reason: "From their ends" means from the whole extent of the group, from among them all (Genesis 47:2). It stresses that the five were picked as the best from the whole tribe, not that they came from its edges.

decisions.choice: men of valor: capable and brave men, fit for hard service
decisions.reason: "Sons of strength" describes men who are able and courageous, often as fighters (Judges 3:29; 20:44). The task needs men who can travel through strange country and judge what they see.

decisions.choice: Zorah and Eshtaol; to spy out the land: Samson's country, and an echo of the spies of Moses and Joshua
decisions.reason: Zorah and Eshtaol are the towns of Samson's family (13:2, 25; 16:31). Sending men to spy out a land before taking it recalls the twelve spies (Numbers 13:2, 17) and the two spies sent to Jericho (Joshua 2:1). The report the five bring back (verses 9-10) is shaped like those earlier reports.

decisions.choice: the Danites; the people of Dan
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "the sons of Dan" with the gender setting, as the whole tribe sends the men. Balanced and Readable say "the Danites" or "the people of Dan", which already include everyone and need no setting.

source.text: הֵ֚מָּה עִם־בֵּ֣ית מִיכָ֔ה וְהֵ֣מָּה הִכִּ֔ירוּ אֶת־ק֥וֹל הַנַּ֖עַר הַלֵּוִ֑י וַיָּס֣וּרוּ שָׁ֗ם וַיֹּ֤אמְרוּ לוֹ֙ מִֽי־הֱבִיאֲךָ֣ הֲלֹ֔ם וּמָֽה־אַתָּ֥ה עֹשֶׂ֛ה בָּזֶ֖ה וּמַה־לְּךָ֥ פֹֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: They [were] near [the] house of Micah, and they recognized [the] voice of the young man the Levite; and they turned aside there and said to him, Who brought you here? And what [are] you doing in this [place]? And what [is] to you here?

en.L: They [were] near the house of Micah, and they recognized the voice of the young man, the Levite. And they turned aside there and said to him, "Who brought you here? And what are you doing in this [place]? And what [is there] for you here?"
en.B: Near Micah's house they recognized the young Levite's voice, so they turned aside there. "Who brought you here?" they asked him. "What are you doing in this place? What is your business here?"
en.R: When they got close to Micah's house, they knew the young Levite's voice. So they went over to him and asked, "Who brought you here? What are you doing in a place like this? Why are you here?"

sw.L: Wao [walikuwa] karibu na nyumba ya Mika, nao wakaitambua sauti ya yule kijana, Mlawi. Nao wakageuka kando huko, wakamwambia, "Ni nani aliyekuleta hapa? Na unafanya nini mahali hapa? Na una [nini] hapa?"
sw.B: Walipokuwa karibu na nyumba ya Mika, waliitambua sauti ya yule kijana Mlawi, kwa hiyo wakageuka kando kwenda huko. Wakamwuliza, "Ni nani aliyekuleta hapa? Unafanya nini mahali hapa? Una shughuli gani hapa?"
sw.R: Walipokaribia nyumba ya Mika, waliitambua sauti ya yule kijana Mlawi. Kwa hiyo walimwendea, wakamwuliza, "Ni nani aliyekuleta hapa? Unafanya nini mahali kama hapa? Kwa nini uko hapa?"

decisions.choice: recognized the voice: either they had known him before, or they knew his speech as that of a man from their own region
decisions.reason: The Hebrew does not say how they recognized him. They may have met him before, or his way of speaking may have marked him as a man from Judah near their own country, since he came from Bethlehem in Judah (17:7) and the Danites lived on the edge of Judah. Their questions suggest surprise at finding him so far from home.

decisions.choice: the young man: the young Levite of 17:7-13
decisions.reason: The word names a young man, and sometimes an attendant. Here it refers to the young Levite Micah had hired as his priest (17:7, 12), the same man the Danites will take with them.

decisions.choice: What is your business here; Why are you here
decisions.reason: "What is to you here" asks what he has to do in the place. Balanced says "What is your business here?" and Readable "Why are you here?", both natural ways of asking the same thing.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֔ם כָּזֹ֣ה וְכָזֶ֔ה עָ֥שָׂה לִ֖י מִיכָ֑ה וַיִּשְׂכְּרֵ֕נִי וָאֱהִי־ל֖וֹ לְכֹהֵֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said to them, Like this and like this has done to me Micah, and he hired me, and I became for him for a priest.

en.L: And he said to them, "Thus and thus Micah has done for me: he hired me, and I have become his priest."
en.B: He told them, "This is what Micah has done for me: he hired me, and I have become his priest."
en.R: He told them what Micah had done for him. "He hired me," he said, "and now I am his priest."

sw.L: Naye akawaambia, "Hivi na hivi ndivyo Mika alivyonitendea: ameniajiri, nami nimekuwa kuhani wake."
sw.B: Aliwaambia, "Hivi ndivyo Mika alivyonitendea: ameniajiri, nami nimekuwa kuhani wake."
sw.R: Aliwaeleza yale Mika aliyomtendea. Alisema, "Aliniajiri, na sasa mimi ni kuhani wake."

decisions.choice: thus and thus: a short way of reporting a longer account
decisions.reason: "Like this and like this" stands for details the narrator does not repeat (2 Samuel 17:15; 1 Kings 14:5). The reader already knows them from 17:7-13.

decisions.choice: he hired me: he serves as priest for wages
decisions.reason: Micah pays him ten pieces of silver a year with clothing and food (17:10). The word "hired" is blunt: he is a priest for pay, which prepares for verses 19-20, where he takes a better offer.

decisions.choice: He told them what Micah had done for him
decisions.reason: Readable turns the summary "thus and thus" into reported speech and keeps the rest as his own words, so the reader is not left with a phrase that says nothing.

source.text: וַיֹּ֥אמְרוּ ל֖וֹ שְׁאַל־נָ֣א בֵאלֹהִ֑ים וְנֵ֣דְעָ֔ה הֲתַצְלִ֣יחַ דַּרְכֵּ֔נוּ אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲנַ֖חְנוּ הֹלְכִ֥ים עָלֶֽיהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And they said to him, Ask, please, of God, and let us know whether will succeed our way which we [are] going on it.

en.L: And they said to him, "Inquire of God, please, so that we may know whether our way on which we are going will succeed."
en.B: They said to him, "Please inquire of God, so that we may know whether this journey we are on will succeed."
en.R: They said, "Please ask God for us. We want to know if our trip will be successful."

sw.L: Nao wakamwambia, "Tafadhali utuulizie kwa Mungu, ili tujue kama njia yetu tunayoiendea itafanikiwa."
sw.B: Walimwambia, "Tafadhali utuulizie kwa Mungu, ili tujue kama safari hii tunayoifanya itafanikiwa."
sw.R: Walisema, "Tafadhali tuulizie kwa Mungu. Tunataka kujua kama safari yetu itafanikiwa."

decisions.choice: inquire of God: seek an answer from God through the priest
decisions.reason: Asking of God was a priest's task, often with the ephod (1 Samuel 23:9-12; 30:7-8). Micah's shrine had an ephod and teraphim (17:5), and the Danites expect the priest to use them to get an answer.

decisions.choice: God: the general word for God
decisions.reason: The Danites use the common word for God, not the name of the LORD. The same word can also mean "gods", but here it takes a singular sense, as in verse 10; in the priest's reply (verse 6) the LORD is named.

decisions.choice: will our way succeed: will the journey reach its goal
decisions.reason: The verb means to go well, to prosper (Genesis 24:21, 40). "Our way" is the journey they are on, with its purpose of finding land.

decisions.choice: ask God for us
decisions.reason: Readable adds "for us", which the request implies: the priest is to ask on their behalf.

source.text: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר לָהֶ֛ם הַכֹּהֵ֖ן לְכ֣וּ לְשָׁל֑וֹם נֹ֣כַח יְהוָ֔ה דַּרְכְּכֶ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר תֵּֽלְכוּ־בָֽהּ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And said to them the priest, Go in peace; before Yahweh [is] your way which you go on it.

en.L: And the priest said to them, "Go in peace. Your way on which you go [is] before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."
en.B: The priest answered them, "Go in peace. The journey you are making is under the eye of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."
en.R: The priest said, "Go in peace. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} eye on the trip you are taking."

sw.L: Naye kuhani akawaambia, "Nendeni kwa amani. Njia yenu mnayoiendea [iko] mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}."
sw.B: Kuhani aliwajibu, "Nendeni kwa amani. Safari mnayoifanya iko chini ya macho ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}."
sw.R: Kuhani alisema, "Nendeni kwa amani. {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ameweka jicho {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} juu ya safari mnayoifanya."

decisions.choice: before the LORD: the LORD has the journey in view
decisions.reason: "In front of the LORD" means in his sight (Proverbs 5:21). It is usually heard as a promise that the LORD watches over the journey with favor, and that is how the Danites take it. But the words do not say outright that the LORD approves, and the priest gives no sign of having consulted anyone. The answer may be meant to sound good without promising much.

decisions.choice: the LORD: the priest uses the divine name
decisions.reason: The Danites asked "God" (verse 5); the priest answers with the name of the LORD, the God of Israel, even though he serves at a shrine with images (17:3-5).

decisions.choice: under the eye of the LORD; has his eye on
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say the journey is in the LORD's sight without making the answer more favorable than the Hebrew does (m1).

source.text: וַיֵּלְכוּ֙ חֲמֵ֣שֶׁת הָאֲנָשִׁ֔ים וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ לָ֑יְשָׁה וַיִּרְא֣וּ אֶת־הָעָ֣ם אֲשֶׁר־בְּקִרְבָּ֣הּ יוֹשֶֽׁבֶת־לָ֠בֶטַח כְּמִשְׁפַּ֨ט צִדֹנִ֜ים שֹׁקֵ֣ט׀וּבֹטֵ֗חַ וְאֵין־מַכְלִ֨ים דָּבָ֤ר בָּאָ֨רֶץ֙ יוֹרֵ֣שׁ עֶ֔צֶר וּרְחֹקִ֥ים הֵ֨מָּה֙ מִצִּ֣דֹנִ֔ים וְדָבָ֥ר אֵין־לָהֶ֖ם עִם־אָדָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And went the five men and came to Laish, and they saw the people who [were] in its midst dwelling in security, according to [the] manner of [the] Sidonians, quiet and secure, and there [was] none putting to shame anything in the land, possessing restraint, and far [were] they from [the] Sidonians, and a word there [was] not to them with man.

en.L: And the five men went and came to Laish, and they saw the people who were in it living in security, after the manner of the Sidonians, quiet and secure. And there was no one in the land putting [them] to shame in anything, possessing restraint; and they were far from the Sidonians, and they had no dealings with anyone.
en.B: So the five men went on and came to Laish. They saw that the people there were living in security, in the way of the Sidonians, quiet and unsuspecting. No one in the land held power over them or did them harm in any way. They lived far from the Sidonians and had no dealings with anyone.
en.R: So the five men left and went to the town of Laish. They saw that its people felt safe there. They lived like the people of Sidon, quiet and not expecting any trouble. No ruler in the land troubled them in any way. They lived far from the Sidonians and had nothing to do with anyone else.

sw.L: Basi wale watu watano wakaenda, wakafika Laishi, wakawaona watu waliokuwa ndani yake wakikaa salama, kwa desturi ya Wasidoni, wametulia na salama. Wala hapakuwa na mtu katika nchi aliyewaaibisha katika jambo lolote, mwenye mamlaka; nao walikuwa mbali na Wasidoni, wala hawakuwa na shughuli na mtu yeyote.
sw.B: Basi wale watu watano waliendelea, wakafika Laishi. Waliona kwamba watu wa huko waliishi salama, kwa namna ya Wasidoni, wametulia na bila wasiwasi. Hakuna mtu katika nchi aliyewatawala wala kuwadhuru kwa namna yoyote. Waliishi mbali na Wasidoni, wala hawakuwa na shughuli na mtu yeyote.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo wale watu watano waliondoka, wakaenda mpaka mji wa Laishi. Waliona kwamba watu wake walijisikia salama huko. Waliishi kama watu wa Sidoni, wametulia na bila kutazamia taabu yoyote. Hakuna mtawala katika nchi aliyewasumbua kwa njia yoyote. Waliishi mbali na Wasidoni, wala hawakuwa na uhusiano na mtu mwingine yeyote.

decisions.choice: Laish, after the manner of the Sidonians: a peaceful town in the far north
decisions.reason: Laish, also called Leshem (Joshua 19:47), lay at the far north of the land, near the springs of the Jordan. The Sidonians were the people of the coastal city of Sidon, known for trade rather than war. To live in their manner is to live at ease, without walls or an army ready for attack.

decisions.choice: no one in the land putting them to shame in anything, possessing restraint: no ruler held power over them or wronged them
alternatives: they lacked nothing in the land, and had wealth
decisions.reason: This clause is hard. The verb means to put to shame or to harm, and "possessing restraint" most likely means holding power to restrain, that is, a ruler. Read so, nobody in the land oppressed them or held power over them. Another reading takes the clause with verse 10 to mean that they lacked nothing in the land. Either way it adds to the picture of an undefended, carefree people.

decisions.choice: far from the Sidonians, with no dealings with anyone: no allies who would come to help
decisions.reason: Laish was far from Sidon and had no treaty or ties with any other people. The point becomes plain in verse 28: when Laish is attacked, no one comes to rescue it.

decisions.choice: with anyone: the Hebrew reads "man"; some Greek copies read "Aram"
alternatives: they had no dealings with Aram
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word for "man, anyone" differs from the name Aram (Syria) by one similar letter, and some copies of the Greek translation read "with Aram" here and in verse 28. Aram lay near Laish, so that reading would say they had no ties with their nearest powerful neighbor. The Hebrew reading makes the wider point that they had no ties with anyone. Reviewers should check the evidence.

decisions.choice: unsuspecting; not expecting any trouble
decisions.reason: The word for "secure" also means trusting, off guard. Literal keeps "secure"; Balanced says "unsuspecting" and Readable "not expecting any trouble", which bring out what the spies notice: the town is open to attack.

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ אֶל־אֲחֵיהֶ֔ם צָרְעָ֖ה וְאֶשְׁתָּאֹ֑ל וַיֹּאמְר֥וּ לָהֶ֛ם אֲחֵיהֶ֖ם מָ֥ה אַתֶּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And they came to their brothers [at] Zorah and Eshtaol, and said to them their brothers, What [are] you?

en.L: And they came to their brothers [at] Zorah and Eshtaol, and their brothers said to them, "What [about] you?"
en.B: When they came back to their kinsmen at Zorah and Eshtaol, their kinsmen asked them, "What news do you bring?"
en.R: Then they returned to the people of their tribe at Zorah and Eshtaol. "What did you find?" the people asked them.

sw.L: Nao wakafika kwa ndugu zao [huko] Sora na Eshtaoli, na ndugu zao wakawaambia, "Je, ninyi [mmeonaje]?"
sw.B: Waliporudi kwa ndugu zao huko Sora na Eshtaoli, ndugu zao waliwauliza, "Mna habari gani?"
sw.R: Kisha walirudi kwa watu wa kabila lao huko Sora na Eshtaoli. Watu hao waliwauliza, "Mmeona nini?"

decisions.choice: what are you: how did it go, what is your report
decisions.reason: The bare question "What you?" asks for news of how things went (compare Ruth 3:16). The Danites want to hear what the spies found.

decisions.choice: kinsmen; the people of their tribe
decisions.reason: "Brothers" here means fellow Danites. Literal keeps "brothers"; Balanced says "kinsmen" and Readable "the people of their tribe".

source.text: וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ ק֚וּמָה וְנַעֲלֶ֣ה עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם כִּ֤י רָאִ֨ינוּ֙ אֶת־הָאָ֔רֶץ וְהִנֵּ֥ה טוֹבָ֖ה מְאֹ֑ד וְאַתֶּ֣ם מַחְשִׁ֔ים אַל־תֵּעָ֣צְל֔וּ לָלֶ֥כֶת לָבֹ֖א לָרֶ֥שֶׁת אֶת־הָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: And they said, Arise, and let us go up against them, for we have seen the land, and behold, [it is] good, very; and you [are] keeping still! Do not be sluggish to go, to come in to possess the land.

en.L: And they said, "Arise, and let us go up against them, for we have seen the land, and look, [it is] very good. And you are keeping still! Do not be slow to go, to enter, to take possession of the land.
en.B: They answered, "Come on, let us go up against them! We have seen the land, and it is very good. And here you sit doing nothing! Do not be slow to go in and take possession of the land.
en.R: "Come on, let us attack them!" they said. "We have seen the land, and it is very good. And you are doing nothing! Do not wait. Go in and take the land for yourselves.

sw.L: Nao wakasema, "Inukeni, tupande juu yao, kwa maana tumeiona nchi, na tazama, [ni] nzuri sana. Nanyi mnakaa kimya! Msiwe wavivu kwenda, kuingia ili kuimiliki nchi.
sw.B: Walijibu, "Haya, tupande tukawashambulie! Tumeiona nchi, nayo ni nzuri sana. Nanyi mnakaa tu bila kufanya lolote! Msikawie kwenda kuingia na kuimiliki nchi hiyo.
sw.R: Walisema, "Haya, twende tukawashambulie! Tumeiona nchi, nayo ni nzuri sana. Nanyi hamfanyi lolote! Msingoje. Ingieni mkaichukue nchi iwe yenu.

decisions.choice: we have seen the land, it is very good: an echo of the reports of the first spies
decisions.reason: Joshua and Caleb said of Canaan, "the land is very, very good" (Numbers 14:7), and the people were told to go up and take possession (Deuteronomy 1:21, 25). The Danite spies use the same kind of words, but the land they urge their people to take is a quiet town at the edge of the land, not the share given them by lot.

decisions.choice: you are keeping still: a rebuke of the people's delay
decisions.reason: The verb describes being silent or doing nothing. Set beside "Arise" and "do not be slow", it scolds the Danites for staying where they are while a good land waits.

decisions.choice: Come on
decisions.reason: "Arise" here is a call to action, not to stand up. Balanced and Readable say "Come on". Literal keeps "Arise".

source.text: כְּבֹאֲכֶ֞ם תָּבֹ֣אוּ׀אֶל־עַ֣ם בֹּטֵ֗חַ וְהָאָ֨רֶץ֙ רַחֲבַ֣ת יָדַ֔יִם כִּֽי־נְתָנָ֥הּ אֱלֹהִ֖ים בְּיֶדְכֶ֑ם מָקוֹם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֵֽין־שָׁ֣ם מַחְס֔וֹר כָּל־דָּבָ֖ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר בָּאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: When you come you will come to a people secure, and the land [is] broad of hands, for has given it God into your hand, a place where there [is] not there lack of any thing which [is] on the earth.

en.L: When you go, you will come to a people secure, and the land [is] wide on both sides, for God has given it into your hand, a place where there is no lack of anything that is on the earth."
en.B: When you go, you will come to an unsuspecting people and a spacious land. God has given it into your hands, a place that lacks nothing on earth."
en.R: When you get there, you will find people who are not expecting trouble. The land is large. God has given it to you. It is a place that has everything anyone could want."

sw.L: Mtakapokwenda, mtafika kwa watu walio salama, na nchi [ni] pana pande zote, kwa maana Mungu ameitia mkononi mwenu, mahali ambapo hapakosekani kitu chochote kilichoko duniani."
sw.B: Mtakapokwenda, mtafika kwa watu wasio na wasiwasi na nchi kubwa. Mungu ameitia mikononi mwenu, mahali pasipokosa kitu chochote duniani."
sw.R: Mtakapofika huko, mtakuta watu ambao hawatazamii taabu. Nchi ni kubwa. Mungu amewapa ninyi. Ni mahali penye kila kitu ambacho mtu angeweza kutaka."

decisions.choice: broad of hands: wide in every direction, spacious
decisions.reason: "Hands" here means sides. A land "broad of hands" stretches out widely on both sides (Genesis 34:21; Isaiah 33:21).

decisions.choice: God has given it into your hand: the spies claim the land with words used of the conquest
decisions.reason: "Given into your hand" is the language of God handing over a land or an enemy (Joshua 2:24; Judges 1:2). The spies base it on the priest's answer (verse 6). The narrator does not say that God gave the land; the reader must weigh the claim against the story.

decisions.choice: on the earth: anything in the whole world
decisions.reason: The same word means "land" and "earth". Here "anything that is on the earth" means anything at all: the place lacks nothing.

decisions.choice: unsuspecting; not expecting trouble
decisions.reason: As in verse 7.

source.text: וַיִּסְע֤וּ מִשָּׁם֙ מִמִּשְׁפַּ֣חַת הַדָּנִ֔י מִצָּרְעָ֖ה וּמֵאֶשְׁתָּאֹ֑ל שֵֽׁשׁ־מֵא֣וֹת אִ֔ישׁ חָג֖וּר כְּלֵ֥י מִלְחָמָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And set out from there, from [the] clan of the Danite[s], from Zorah and from Eshtaol, six hundred man girded [with] weapons of war.

en.L: And there set out from there, from the clan of the Danites, from Zorah and from Eshtaol, 600 men girded with weapons of war.
en.B: So 600 men of the clan of the Danites, armed with weapons of war, set out from there, from Zorah and Eshtaol.
en.R: So 600 men from the tribe of Dan set out from Zorah and Eshtaol. They were armed and ready for war.

sw.L: Wakaondoka huko, kutoka ukoo wa Wadani, kutoka Sora na kutoka Eshtaoli, watu 600 waliojifunga silaha za vita.
sw.B: Basi watu 600 wa ukoo wa Wadani, wakiwa na silaha za vita, waliondoka huko, kutoka Sora na Eshtaoli.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo watu 600 wa kabila la Dani waliondoka Sora na Eshtaoli. Walikuwa na silaha, tayari kwa vita.

decisions.choice: girded with weapons of war: armed for battle
decisions.reason: To "gird" is to fasten on, as a sword is fastened to the belt (3:16). The men go out armed and ready to fight.

decisions.choice: 600 men: the fighting men of the group that moved
decisions.reason: The census counts many more fighting men in Dan (Numbers 26:43), so the 600 are probably the armed men of the part of the tribe that moved north. They travel with their families and animals (verse 21).

decisions.choice: the tribe of Dan
decisions.reason: Readable says "tribe" for the clan of the Danites, since in this chapter the clan is the whole tribe (verse 2).

source.text: וַֽיַּעֲל֗וּ וַֽיַּחֲנ֛וּ בְּקִרְיַ֥ת יְעָרִ֖ים בִּֽיהוּדָ֑ה עַל־כֵּ֡ן קָרְאוּ֩ לַמָּק֨וֹם הַה֜וּא מַחֲנֵה־דָ֗ן עַ֚ד הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה הִנֵּ֕ה אַחֲרֵ֖י קִרְיַ֥ת יְעָרִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And they went up and encamped at Kiriath-jearim in Judah; therefore they called that place Mahaneh-dan until this day; behold, [it is] behind Kiriath-jearim.

en.L: And they went up and camped at Kiriath-jearim in Judah. Therefore they called that place Mahaneh-dan to this day; look, [it is] behind Kiriath-jearim.
en.B: They went up and made camp at Kiriath-jearim in Judah. This is why the place west of Kiriath-jearim has been called Mahaneh-dan to this day.
en.R: They went up and set up camp near the town of Kiriath-jearim in Judah. That is why the place just west of Kiriath-jearim is called Mahaneh-dan to this day. The name means "Dan's Camp."

sw.L: Wakapanda, wakapiga kambi Kiriath-yearimu katika Yuda. Kwa hiyo wakapaita mahali pale Mahane-dani mpaka leo; tazama, [pako] nyuma ya Kiriath-yearimu.
sw.B: Walipanda, wakapiga kambi Kiriath-yearimu katika Yuda. Ndiyo sababu mahali palipo magharibi ya Kiriath-yearimu panaitwa Mahane-dani mpaka leo.
sw.R: Walipanda, wakapiga kambi karibu na mji wa Kiriath-yearimu katika Yuda. Ndiyo sababu mahali palipo upande wa magharibi wa Kiriath-yearimu panaitwa Mahane-dani mpaka leo. Jina hilo maana yake "Kambi ya Dani."

decisions.choice: Mahaneh-dan: "the camp of Dan"
decisions.reason: The name means "camp of Dan". A place with the same name is placed between Zorah and Eshtaol in 13:25. The name may have been used for more than one Danite campsite in this area, or for one area near both; the Hebrew does not explain.

decisions.choice: behind Kiriath-jearim: west of it
decisions.reason: Directions in Hebrew are given facing east, toward the sunrise, so "behind" means west (compare Isaiah 9:11, where "behind" stands for the west).

decisions.choice: to this day: in the narrator's own time
decisions.reason: The narrator explains a place name still known to the first readers, as often in Joshua and Judges (Joshua 7:26; Judges 1:26).

decisions.choice: west of
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "behind"; Balanced and Readable say "west of" (m2). Readable also gives the meaning of the name.

source.text: וַיַּעַבְר֥וּ מִשָּׁ֖ם הַר־אֶפְרָ֑יִם וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ עַד־בֵּ֥ית מִיכָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And they passed from there [to the] hill country of Ephraim and came to [the] house of Micah.

en.L: And they passed on from there to the hill country of Ephraim and came to the house of Micah.
en.B: From there they went on into the hill country of Ephraim and came to Micah's house.
en.R: From there they traveled on into the hills of Ephraim and came to Micah's house.

sw.L: Nao wakapita kutoka huko mpaka nchi ya milima ya Efraimu, wakafika kwenye nyumba ya Mika.
sw.B: Kutoka huko waliendelea mpaka nchi ya milima ya Efraimu, wakafika kwenye nyumba ya Mika.
sw.R: Kutoka huko walisafiri kuingia katika milima ya Efraimu, wakafika kwenye nyumba ya Mika.

decisions.choice: to the house of Micah: the army takes the same road as the spies
decisions.reason: The words repeat verse 2, where the five spies came to the same house. The reader knows what the army will find there.

decisions.choice: the hills of Ephraim
decisions.reason: Readable says "the hills of Ephraim", as in 17:1.

source.text: וַֽיַּעֲנ֞וּ חֲמֵ֣שֶׁת הָאֲנָשִׁ֗ים הַהֹלְכִים֮ לְרַגֵּל֮ אֶת־הָאָ֣רֶץ לַיִשׁ֒ וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ אֶל־אֲחֵיהֶ֔ם הַיְדַעְתֶּ֗ם כִּ֠י יֵ֣שׁ בַּבָּתִּ֤ים הָאֵ֨לֶּה֙ אֵפ֣וֹד וּתְרָפִ֔ים וּפֶ֖סֶל וּמַסֵּכָ֑ה וְעַתָּ֖ה דְּע֥וּ מַֽה־תַּעֲשֽׂוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And answered the five men who had gone to spy out the land [of] Laish, and said to their brothers, Do you know that there is in the houses the these an ephod and teraphim and a carved image and a molten image? And now, know what you will do.

en.L: And the five men who had gone to spy out the land, Laish, spoke up and said to their brothers, "Do you know that in these houses there are an ephod and household gods, and a carved image and a cast idol? And now, consider what you will do."
en.B: Then the five men who had spied out the land of Laish said to their kinsmen, "Did you know that in these houses there is an ephod, household gods, a carved image and a cast idol? Now think about what you should do."
en.R: Then the five men who had spied out the land around Laish spoke to the other men of their tribe. "Did you know that in these houses there is an ephod, a holy object used in worship?" they said. "There are also household idols, a carved idol and an idol of melted metal. Now think about what you should do."

sw.L: Nao wale watu watano waliokwenda kuipeleleza nchi, Laishi, wakajibu, wakawaambia ndugu zao, "Je, mnajua ya kuwa katika nyumba hizi kuna efodi na terafimu, na sanamu ya kuchonga na sanamu ya kusubu? Basi sasa fikirini mtakalofanya."
sw.B: Kisha wale watu watano walioipeleleza nchi ya Laishi waliwaambia ndugu zao, "Je, mnajua kwamba katika nyumba hizi kuna efodi, miungu ya nyumbani, sanamu ya kuchonga na sanamu ya kusubu? Sasa fikirini mnachopaswa kufanya."
sw.R: Kisha wale watu watano walioichunguza nchi ya kando ya Laishi waliwaambia watu wengine wa kabila lao, "Je, mnajua kwamba katika nyumba hizi kuna efodi, kitu kitakatifu kinachotumika katika ibada? Kuna pia sanamu za miungu ya nyumbani, sanamu ya kuchonga na sanamu ya chuma kilichoyeyushwa. Sasa fikirini mnachopaswa kufanya."

decisions.choice: answered: spoke up
decisions.reason: The verb "answer" often means simply to begin speaking in response to a situation, with no question asked before it (Deuteronomy 21:7).

decisions.choice: these houses: Micah's homestead, a group of houses
decisions.reason: Micah's place was a cluster of buildings, a family compound with a gate (verse 16). Micah's shrine stood there, and the Levite had a house of his own within it (verse 15). Neighbors lived in houses nearby (verse 22).

decisions.choice: an ephod, household gods, a carved image and a cast idol: the objects of Micah's shrine
decisions.reason: These are the things made in 17:3-5. The ephod was a priestly garment or object used to seek answers from God. The household gods (teraphim) were small figures kept in a home (Genesis 31:19). The carved image and the cast idol were made from the silver Micah's mother dedicated. The chapter lists them in different orders (verses 17, 18, 20) but means the same set.

decisions.choice: consider what you will do: a hint that the Danites should take them
decisions.reason: The spies do not say outright what to do, but the question points to one answer: seize the shrine. The next verses show that this is how it was understood.

decisions.choice: a holy object used in worship
decisions.reason: Readable explains the ephod the first time it appears in the chapter, as in 17:5, and splits the long question into two sentences.

source.text: וַיָּס֣וּרוּ שָׁ֔מָּה וַיָּבֹ֛אוּ אֶל־בֵּֽית־הַנַּ֥עַר הַלֵּוִ֖י בֵּ֣ית מִיכָ֑ה וַיִּשְׁאֲלוּ־ל֖וֹ לְשָׁלֽוֹם׃

records.literal_gloss: And they turned aside there and came to [the] house of the young man the Levite, [the] house of Micah, and asked him of welfare.

en.L: And they turned aside there and came to the house of the young man, the Levite, at the house of Micah, and asked him of [his] welfare.
en.B: So they turned aside there, came to the young Levite's house at Micah's place, and greeted him.
en.R: So they went over to the house where the young Levite lived, at Micah's place, and greeted him.

sw.L: Nao wakageuka kando huko, wakafika kwenye nyumba ya yule kijana, Mlawi, nyumbani kwa Mika, wakamjulia hali.
sw.B: Basi waligeuka kando huko, wakafika kwenye nyumba ya yule kijana Mlawi nyumbani kwa Mika, wakamsalimu.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo walikwenda kwenye nyumba alimoishi yule kijana Mlawi, nyumbani kwa Mika, wakamsalimu.

decisions.choice: asked him of welfare: greeted him
decisions.reason: To ask about someone's peace or welfare is the usual greeting (Genesis 43:27; Exodus 18:7). The five greet the Levite as men he already knows (verse 3).

decisions.choice: the house of the Levite, the house of Micah: the Levite's lodging inside Micah's homestead
decisions.reason: The two phrases stand side by side. The Levite's house was part of Micah's household (17:12), so both names describe the same place.

decisions.choice: greeted him
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the greeting (m1). Literal keeps "asked him of his welfare".

source.text: וְשֵׁשׁ־מֵא֣וֹת אִ֗ישׁ חֲגוּרִים֙ כְּלֵ֣י מִלְחַמְתָּ֔ם נִצָּבִ֖ים פֶּ֣תַח הַשָּׁ֑עַר אֲשֶׁ֖ר מִבְּנֵי־דָֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And six hundred man girded [with] their weapons of war [were] standing [at the] entrance of the gate, who [were] of [the] sons of Dan.

en.L: And 600 men girded with their weapons of war were standing at the entrance of the gate, who were of the sons of Dan.
en.B: Meanwhile the 600 armed men of Dan stood at the entrance of the gate.
en.R: All the while, the 600 men from Dan stood at the gate, armed for war.

sw.L: Nao wale watu 600 waliojifunga silaha zao za vita walikuwa wamesimama kwenye mlango wa lango, ambao [walikuwa] wa wana wa Dani.
sw.B: Wakati huo wale watu 600 wa Dani wenye silaha walisimama kwenye mlango wa lango.
sw.R: Muda wote huo wale watu 600 wa Dani walisimama langoni, wakiwa na silaha tayari kwa vita.

decisions.choice: were standing at the entrance of the gate: background to what happens inside
decisions.reason: The sentence breaks the run of events to describe the scene: while the five men greet the Levite, the armed band waits at the gate of the homestead. Their presence is a threat, and it explains why no one stops what follows (verses 17-18).

decisions.choice: the gate: the entrance of Micah's homestead
decisions.reason: The gate is the entrance to the walled yard of Micah's compound, not a town gate. Standing there, the 600 control who goes in and out.

decisions.choice: the sons of Dan
decisions.reason: Here and in verses 22-26 "sons of Dan" means the armed band, so Literal has no gender setting; Balanced and Readable say "men of Dan" or "the Danites".

source.text: וַֽיַּעֲל֞וּ חֲמֵ֣שֶׁת הָאֲנָשִׁ֗ים הַהֹלְכִים֮ לְרַגֵּ֣ל אֶת־הָאָרֶץ֒ בָּ֣אוּ שָׁ֔מָּה לָקְח֗וּ אֶת־הַפֶּ֨סֶל֙ וְאֶת־הָ֣אֵפ֔וֹד וְאֶת־הַתְּרָפִ֖ים וְאֶת־הַמַּסֵּכָ֑ה וְהַכֹּהֵ֗ן נִצָּב֙ פֶּ֣תַח הַשַּׁ֔עַר וְשֵׁשׁ־מֵא֣וֹת הָאִ֔ישׁ הֶחָג֖וּר כְּלֵ֥י הַמִּלְחָמָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And went up the five men who had gone to spy out the land; they came in there; they took the carved image and the ephod and the teraphim and the molten image; and the priest [was] standing [at the] entrance of the gate, and the six hundred the man the girded [with] the weapons of war.

en.L: And the five men who had gone to spy out the land went up; they went in there; they took the carved image and the ephod and the household gods and the cast idol, while the priest [was] standing at the entrance of the gate with the 600 men girded with weapons of war.
en.B: The five men who had spied out the land went up, entered the house, and took the carved image, the ephod, the household gods and the cast idol, while the priest was standing at the gate's entrance with the 600 armed men.
en.R: The five men who had spied out the land went up into the house. They took the carved idol, the ephod, the household idols, and the idol of melted metal. All this time the priest was standing at the gate with the 600 armed men.

sw.L: Nao wale watu watano waliokwenda kuipeleleza nchi wakapanda; wakaingia humo; wakaitwaa sanamu ya kuchonga na efodi na terafimu na sanamu ya kusubu, kuhani akiwa amesimama kwenye mlango wa lango pamoja na wale watu 600 waliojifunga silaha za vita.
sw.B: Wale watu watano walioipeleleza nchi walipanda, wakaingia ndani ya nyumba, wakaichukua sanamu ya kuchonga, efodi, miungu ya nyumbani na sanamu ya kusubu, huku kuhani akiwa amesimama kwenye mlango wa lango pamoja na wale watu 600 wenye silaha.
sw.R: Wale watu watano walioichunguza nchi walipanda kuingia ndani ya nyumba. Walichukua sanamu ya kuchonga, efodi, sanamu za miungu ya nyumbani, na sanamu ya chuma kilichoyeyushwa. Muda wote huo kuhani alikuwa amesimama langoni pamoja na wale watu 600 wenye silaha.

decisions.choice: went in there, took: quick action, told without "and"
decisions.reason: The verbs follow one another without the usual "and", which makes the scene move fast: in, take, done.

decisions.choice: the priest was standing at the gate with the 600: he was outside while the shrine was emptied
decisions.reason: The five had greeted the priest (verse 15), and he stayed talking with the armed men at the gate while the five went in. Verse 18 goes back over the same moment, when he notices what they are doing.

decisions.choice: entered the house; into the house
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "the house" for "there", the place where the objects were kept.

source.text: וְאֵ֗לֶּה בָּ֚אוּ בֵּ֣ית מִיכָ֔ה וַיִּקְחוּ֙ אֶת־פֶּ֣סֶל הָאֵפ֔וֹד וְאֶת־הַתְּרָפִ֖ים וְאֶת־הַמַּסֵּכָ֑ה וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶם֙ הַכֹּהֵ֔ן מָ֥ה אַתֶּ֖ם עֹשִֽׂים׃

records.literal_gloss: And these came into [the] house of Micah, and took [the] carved image of the ephod and the teraphim and the molten image; and said to them the priest, What [are] you doing?

en.L: And these went into the house of Micah and took the carved image [and] the ephod and the household gods and the cast idol. And the priest said to them, "What are you doing?"
en.B: When these men went into Micah's house and took the carved image, the ephod, the household gods and the cast idol, the priest said to them, "What are you doing?"
en.R: When the men went into Micah's house and took the carved idol, the ephod, the household idols, and the idol of melted metal, the priest asked them, "What are you doing?"

sw.L: Nao hao wakaingia katika nyumba ya Mika, wakaitwaa sanamu ya kuchonga [na] efodi na terafimu na sanamu ya kusubu. Naye kuhani akawaambia, "Mnafanya nini?"
sw.B: Watu hao walipoingia katika nyumba ya Mika na kuichukua sanamu ya kuchonga, efodi, miungu ya nyumbani na sanamu ya kusubu, kuhani aliwaambia, "Mnafanya nini?"
sw.R: Watu hao walipoingia katika nyumba ya Mika na kuchukua sanamu ya kuchonga, efodi, sanamu za miungu ya nyumbani na sanamu ya chuma kilichoyeyushwa, kuhani aliwauliza, "Mnafanya nini?"

decisions.choice: the carved image, the ephod: two objects in a list
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads as if "the carved image of the ephod", but the objects are listed separately in verses 14, 17 and 20, and the word "and" has simply not been written here. The sense is a list of four things.

decisions.choice: these: the five men; the verse tells the same moment again
decisions.reason: "These" are the five spies of verse 17. The verse goes back over their entering and taking, now from the moment the priest sees them and objects.

decisions.choice: When these men went into ..., the priest said
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable join the two clauses with "when", since the priest's question comes as he sees them take the objects.

source.text: וַיֹּאמְרוּ֩ ל֨וֹ הַחֲרֵ֜שׁ שִֽׂים־יָדְךָ֤ עַל־פִּ֨יךָ֙ וְלֵ֣ךְ עִמָּ֔נוּ וֶֽהְיֵה־לָ֖נוּ לְאָ֣ב וּלְכֹהֵ֑ן הֲט֣וֹב׀הֱיוֹתְךָ֣ כֹהֵ֗ן לְבֵית֙ אִ֣ישׁ אֶחָ֔ד א֚וֹ הֱיוֹתְךָ֣ כֹהֵ֔ן לְשֵׁ֥בֶט וּלְמִשְׁפָּחָ֖ה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And they said to him, Be silent, put your hand on your mouth, and go with us and be to us for a father and for a priest; [is it] better your being priest to [the] house of man one or your being priest to a tribe and to a clan in Israel?

en.L: And they said to him, "Keep quiet! Put your hand over your mouth and come with us, and be to us a father and a priest. Is it better for you to be priest to the house of one man, or to be priest to a tribe and a clan in Israel?"
en.B: They answered him, "Be quiet! Put your hand over your mouth and come with us. Be a father and a priest to us. Which is better: to be priest for one man's household, or for a tribe and clan in Israel?"
en.R: "Be quiet!" they told him. "Do not say a word. Come with us and be our adviser and our priest. Would you rather be a priest for one man's family, or for a whole tribe and clan in Israel?"

sw.L: Nao wakamwambia, "Nyamaza! Weka mkono wako juu ya kinywa chako, uende pamoja nasi, uwe kwetu baba na kuhani. Je, ni bora wewe uwe kuhani wa nyumba ya mtu mmoja, au uwe kuhani wa kabila na ukoo katika Israeli?"
sw.B: Walimjibu, "Nyamaza! Weka mkono wako kinywani, uje pamoja nasi. Uwe baba na kuhani kwetu. Ni lipi bora: kuwa kuhani wa jamaa ya mtu mmoja, au wa kabila na ukoo katika Israeli?"
sw.R: Walimwambia, "Nyamaza! Usiseme neno. Njoo pamoja nasi uwe mshauri wetu na kuhani wetu. Je, ungependa kuwa kuhani wa jamaa ya mtu mmoja, au wa kabila zima na ukoo katika Israeli?"

decisions.choice: put your hand over your mouth: say nothing
decisions.reason: Laying a hand over the mouth is a sign of keeping silent (Job 21:5; 40:4; Micah 7:16). It strengthens "Keep quiet!".

decisions.choice: a father: an honored adviser and spiritual guide
decisions.reason: "Father" is a title of respect for a priest or prophet who guides others (17:10; 2 Kings 6:21). The Danites offer him the same place Micah gave him, but over a whole tribe.

decisions.choice: is it better ...?: the question expects the answer that a tribe is better
decisions.reason: The question is an offer: a priest for one household or a priest for a tribe. As 17:10-11 showed, the Levite had come looking for a good place, and the offer is meant to appeal to him.

decisions.choice: Do not say a word; our adviser
decisions.reason: Readable gives the meaning of the gesture (m1) and says "adviser" for "father", as in 17:10.

source.text: וַיִּיטַב֙ לֵ֣ב הַכֹּהֵ֔ן וַיִּקַּח֙ אֶת־הָ֣אֵפ֔וֹד וְאֶת־הַתְּרָפִ֖ים וְאֶת־הַפָּ֑סֶל וַיָּבֹ֖א בְּקֶ֥רֶב הָעָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And was good [the] heart of the priest, and he took the ephod and the teraphim and the carved image, and went in [the] midst of the people.

en.L: And the heart of the priest was glad, and he took the ephod and the household gods and the carved image, and went in the midst of the people.
en.B: The priest was pleased. He took the ephod, the household gods and the carved image, and went along among the people.
en.R: This made the priest happy. He took the ephod, the household idols, and the carved idol, and went along with the people.

sw.L: Na moyo wa kuhani ukafurahi, akaitwaa efodi na terafimu na sanamu ya kuchonga, akaenda katikati ya watu.
sw.B: Kuhani alifurahi. Alichukua efodi, miungu ya nyumbani na sanamu ya kuchonga, akaenda pamoja na watu hao katikati yao.
sw.R: Jambo hili lilimfurahisha kuhani. Alichukua efodi, sanamu za miungu ya nyumbani na sanamu ya kuchonga, akaenda pamoja na watu hao.

decisions.choice: the heart of the priest was glad: he was pleased
decisions.reason: For the heart to be "good" is to be glad or in good spirits (19:6, 9; Ruth 3:7). The priest takes the offer at once.

decisions.choice: he took the ephod: the priest himself joins in the theft
decisions.reason: Now the priest takes the objects with his own hands. The cast idol is not named here; the list may simply be shorter, as the carved image alone is named in verses 30-31.

decisions.choice: in the midst of the people: at the center of the company
decisions.reason: He travels in the middle of the band, where the shrine's priest and its objects would be safest.

decisions.choice: was pleased; made the priest happy
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom (m1); Literal keeps the heart.

source.text: וַיִּפְנ֖וּ וַיֵּלֵ֑כוּ וַיָּשִׂ֨ימוּ אֶת־הַטַּ֧ף וְאֶת־הַמִּקְנֶ֛ה וְאֶת־הַכְּבוּדָּ֖ה לִפְנֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And they turned and went, and put the little ones and the livestock and the valuables before them.

en.L: And they turned and went, and they put the little ones and the livestock and the goods in front of them.
en.B: They turned and set off, putting their children, their livestock and their goods in front of them.
en.R: Then the Danites turned and left. They sent their children, their animals, and their belongings on ahead of them.

sw.L: Nao wakageuka, wakaenda, wakawaweka watoto wadogo na mifugo na mali mbele yao.
sw.B: Waligeuka wakaondoka, wakiwatanguliza watoto wao, mifugo yao na mali zao mbele yao.
sw.R: Kisha Wadani waligeuka wakaondoka. Waliwatanguliza mbele watoto wao, wanyama wao na vitu vyao.

decisions.choice: in front of them: the fighting men march at the rear
decisions.reason: The families and goods go ahead, and the armed men follow behind, between them and anyone who might come after them from Micah's place. The next verse shows that they were right to expect it.

decisions.choice: the little ones: the children, and with them the dependents of the household
decisions.reason: The word means young children, and in lists like this it can stand for all who could not fight, the women and children together (Numbers 32:16-17; Deuteronomy 1:39). The Danites are moving with their whole households.

decisions.choice: the goods: valuable possessions
decisions.reason: The word comes from the root for "heavy" and means valuable things, the wealth and baggage the people carried with them.

decisions.choice: the Danites; on ahead
decisions.reason: Readable names the subject and says "sent ... on ahead" for "put in front of them".

source.text: הֵ֥מָּה הִרְחִ֖יקוּ מִבֵּ֣ית מִיכָ֑ה וְהָאֲנָשִׁ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר בַּבָּתִּים֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ עִם־בֵּ֣ית מִיכָ֔ה נִֽזְעֲק֔וּ וַיַּדְבִּ֖יקוּ אֶת־בְּנֵי־דָֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: They had gone far from [the] house of Micah, and the men who [were] in the houses which [were] near [the] house of Micah were called out, and they overtook [the] sons of Dan.

en.L: They had gone some distance from the house of Micah when the men who were in the houses near the house of Micah were called out, and they overtook the sons of Dan.
en.B: When they had gone some distance from Micah's house, the men who lived in the houses near Micah's were called out, and they caught up with the Danites.
en.R: When the Danites were some distance from Micah's house, Micah called together the men who lived in the houses near his. They caught up with the Danites.

sw.L: Wao walikuwa wamekwenda mbali kidogo na nyumba ya Mika, ndipo watu waliokuwa katika nyumba zilizokuwa karibu na nyumba ya Mika walipoitwa, nao wakawafikia wana wa Dani.
sw.B: Walipokuwa wamekwenda mbali kidogo na nyumba ya Mika, watu waliokaa katika nyumba zilizokuwa karibu na ya Mika waliitwa, nao wakawafikia Wadani.
sw.R: Wadani walipokuwa wamekwenda mbali kidogo na nyumba ya Mika, Mika aliwaita pamoja watu walioishi katika nyumba zilizokuwa karibu na yake. Wakawafikia Wadani.

decisions.choice: were called out: summoned to come out together
decisions.reason: The verb is used for men called together to fight (6:34-35; 7:23). Micah's neighbors are roused to go after the Danites. Verse 23 shows that Micah was the one who called them.

decisions.choice: they had gone some distance: the pursuit begins after a delay
decisions.reason: The opening clause sets the scene: the Danites are already on the road when Micah's neighbors set out, but the slow pace of children and animals (verse 21) lets the pursuers catch up.

decisions.choice: Micah called together
decisions.reason: Readable names Micah as the one who called his neighbors out, which verse 23 makes plain, and turns the passive into an active sentence.

source.text: וַֽיִּקְרְאוּ֙ אֶל־בְּנֵי־דָ֔ן וַיַּסֵּ֖בּוּ פְּנֵיהֶ֑ם וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ לְמִיכָ֔ה מַה־לְּךָ֖ כִּ֥י נִזְעָֽקְתָּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And they called to [the] sons of Dan, and they turned their faces and said to Micah, What [is] to you that you have been called out?

en.L: And they called out to the sons of Dan, and they turned their faces and said to Micah, "What [is] with you, that you have been called out?"
en.B: As they shouted after the Danites, the Danites turned around. "What is the matter with you," they said to Micah, "that you have called out these men?"
en.R: They shouted at the Danites, and the Danites turned around. "What is wrong with you?" they asked Micah. "Why have you called out all these men?"

sw.L: Nao wakawaita wana wa Dani, nao wakageuza nyuso zao, wakamwambia Mika, "Una nini, hata umeitwa pamoja?"
sw.B: Walipowapigia kelele Wadani, Wadani waligeuka. Wakamwambia Mika, "Una nini hata umewaita watu hawa?"
sw.R: Waliwapigia kelele Wadani, nao Wadani wakageuka. Walimwuliza Mika, "Una shida gani? Kwa nini umewaita watu hawa wote?"

decisions.choice: what is with you: what is the matter
decisions.reason: "What is to you?" asks what is wrong or what someone wants (Genesis 21:17; 1 Samuel 11:5). From the Danites it is a show of innocence, as if they had done nothing.

decisions.choice: that you have been called out: that you come out with a band of men
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in verse 22. Said to Micah, it means that he has gathered men and come after them, ready for a fight.

decisions.choice: turned their faces: turned around to face them
decisions.reason: The Danites, marching at the rear (verse 21), turn to face their pursuers.

decisions.choice: you have called out these men
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "you have called out these men" for "you have been called out", which is what the verb means here (m2). Literal keeps the passive.

source.text: וַיֹּ֡אמֶר אֶת־אֱלֹהַי֩ אֲשֶׁר־עָשִׂ֨יתִי לְקַחְתֶּ֧ם וְֽאֶת־הַכֹּהֵ֛ן וַתֵּלְכ֖וּ וּמַה־לִּ֣י ע֑וֹד וּמַה־זֶּ֛ה תֹּאמְר֥וּ אֵלַ֖י מַה־לָּֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, My gods which I made you took, and the priest, and you went; and what [is] to me still? And what [is] this [that] you say to me, What [is] to you?

en.L: And he said, "My gods that I made you have taken, and the priest, and you have gone away. And what [is there] still for me? And how [is it that] you say to me, 'What [is] with you?'"
en.B: He answered, "You have taken the gods I made, and the priest, and gone off. What do I have left? How can you ask me, 'What is the matter with you?'"
en.R: Micah said, "You took the gods I made, and you took the priest, and then you left. What do I have now? How can you ask me, 'What is wrong?'"

sw.L: Naye akasema, "Miungu yangu niliyoifanya mmeichukua, na kuhani, nanyi mmekwenda zenu; nami nimebaki na [nini] tena? Basi mnaniambiaje, 'Una nini?'"
sw.B: Akajibu, "Mmeichukua miungu niliyoifanya, na kuhani, mkaondoka. Nimebaki na nini? Mnawezaje kuniuliza, 'Una nini?'"
sw.R: Mika alisema, "Mliichukua miungu niliyoifanya, mkamchukua kuhani, kisha mkaondoka. Sasa nina nini? Mnawezaje kuniuliza, 'Una shida gani?'"

decisions.choice: my gods that I made: the images of the shrine
decisions.reason: The plural word for "God" here means gods, the images Micah had made (17:4-5). Laban too spoke of "my gods" when his teraphim were stolen (Genesis 31:30). There is a bitter irony in Micah's words: gods that a man made with his own hands can also be carried off by other men (compare Isaiah 44:9-20; 46:1-2).

decisions.choice: what is still for me: what do I have left
decisions.reason: "What is there to me still?" means that he has nothing left: his shrine, his gods and his priest are gone.

decisions.choice: how can you say to me, What is with you: Micah throws their question back at them
decisions.reason: Micah repeats their words from verse 23 and finds them absurd, since they are the ones who robbed him.

decisions.choice: You have taken the gods I made
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew order, which puts "my gods" first for emphasis. Balanced and Readable put the clause in plain order.

source.text: וַיֹּאמְר֤וּ אֵלָיו֙ בְּנֵי־דָ֔ן אַל־תַּשְׁמַ֥ע קוֹלְךָ֖ עִמָּ֑נוּ פֶּֽן־יִפְגְּע֣וּ בָכֶ֗ם אֲנָשִׁים֙ מָ֣רֵי נֶ֔פֶשׁ וְאָסַפְתָּ֥ה נַפְשְׁךָ֖ וְנֶ֥פֶשׁ בֵּיתֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to him [the] sons of Dan, Do not let be heard your voice among us, lest fall upon you men bitter of soul, and you gather your life and [the] life of your household.

en.L: And the sons of Dan said to him, "Do not let your voice be heard among us, lest men bitter of soul fall upon you, and you lose your life and the life of your household."
en.B: The Danites told him, "Do not raise your voice at us, or some hot-tempered men may attack you, and you will lose your life and the lives of your household."
en.R: The Danites said to him, "Do not argue with us. Some of our men have bad tempers. They might attack you, and then you and your family would be killed."

sw.L: Nao wana wa Dani wakamwambia, "Sauti yako isisikike kati yetu, wasije watu wenye uchungu wa roho wakakuangukia, nawe ukapoteza uhai wako na uhai wa watu wa nyumbani mwako."
sw.B: Wadani walimwambia, "Usitupazie sauti, la sivyo watu wenye hasira kali watakushambulia, nawe utapoteza uhai wako na wa watu wa nyumbani mwako."
sw.R: Wadani walimwambia, "Usibishane nasi. Baadhi ya watu wetu wana hasira kali. Wanaweza kukushambulia, kisha wewe na jamaa yako mkauawa."

decisions.choice: men bitter of soul: fierce, angry men
decisions.reason: "Bitter of soul" can describe grief (1 Samuel 1:10), but of fighting men it means fierce and enraged, "like a bear robbed of her cubs" (2 Samuel 17:8).

decisions.choice: gather your life: lose it, be killed
decisions.reason: To have one's life "gathered" is to have it taken away in death (Psalm 26:9; 104:29). The threat includes Micah's whole household.

decisions.choice: do not let your voice be heard, lest ...: a threat in the form of a warning
decisions.reason: The Danites speak as if they were only warning Micah about others, but the men they mean are their own.

decisions.choice: hot-tempered men; have bad tempers
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "bitter of soul"; Balanced and Readable say what it means here (m1).

source.text: וַיֵּלְכ֥וּ בְנֵי־דָ֖ן לְדַרְכָּ֑ם וַיַּ֣רְא מִיכָ֗ה כִּי־חֲזָקִ֥ים הֵ֨מָּה֙ מִמֶּ֔נּוּ וַיִּ֖פֶן וַיָּ֥שָׁב אֶל־בֵּיתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And went [the] sons of Dan on their way; and saw Micah that strong [were] they more than him, and he turned and returned to his house.

en.L: And the sons of Dan went on their way. And Micah saw that they [were] too strong for him, and he turned and went back to his house.
en.B: So the Danites went on their way. Micah saw that they were too strong for him, so he turned around and went back home.
en.R: Then the Danites went on their way. Micah saw that they were too strong for him to fight. So he turned around and went home.

sw.L: Nao wana wa Dani wakaenda zao. Naye Mika akaona ya kuwa wao [ni] wenye nguvu kuliko yeye, akageuka, akarudi nyumbani kwake.
sw.B: Basi Wadani waliendelea na safari yao. Mika aliona kwamba walikuwa na nguvu kuliko yeye, kwa hiyo aligeuka akarudi nyumbani.
sw.R: Kisha Wadani waliendelea na safari yao. Mika aliona kwamba walikuwa na nguvu mno asiweze kupigana nao. Kwa hiyo aligeuka akarudi nyumbani.

decisions.choice: too strong for him: stronger than he could resist
decisions.reason: The comparison means that Micah and his neighbors could not stand against 600 armed men. He gives up and goes home, and he is not mentioned again.

decisions.choice: too strong for him to fight
decisions.reason: Readable adds "to fight", which the comparison implies.

source.text: וְהֵ֨מָּה לָקְח֜וּ אֵ֧ת אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֣ה מִיכָ֗ה וְֽאֶת־הַכֹּהֵן֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָיָה־לוֹ֒ וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ עַל־לַ֗יִשׁ עַל־עַם֙ שֹׁקֵ֣ט וּבֹטֵ֔חַ וַיַּכּ֥וּ אוֹתָ֖ם לְפִי־חָ֑רֶב וְאֶת־הָעִ֖יר שָׂרְפ֥וּ בָאֵֽשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And they took what had made Micah, and the priest who had been his, and came upon Laish, upon a people quiet and secure, and struck them with [the] mouth of [the] sword, and the city they burned with fire.

en.L: And they took what Micah had made, and the priest who had been his, and they came upon Laish, upon a people quiet and secure, and they struck them with the edge of the sword, and they burned the city with fire.
en.B: So they took what Micah had made, along with the priest who had been his, and came to Laish, to a quiet and unsuspecting people. They struck them down with the sword and burned the city.
en.R: So the Danites took the things Micah had made, and the priest who had worked for him. Then they went to Laish and attacked its people, who were quiet and not expecting trouble. They killed them with their swords and burned down the town.

sw.L: Nao wakavitwaa vile alivyovifanya Mika, na kuhani aliyekuwa wake, wakaujia Laishi, watu waliotulia na salama, wakawapiga kwa makali ya upanga, nao mji wakauteketeza kwa moto.
sw.B: Basi walichukua vile Mika alivyovifanya, pamoja na kuhani aliyekuwa wake, wakafika Laishi, kwa watu waliotulia wasio na wasiwasi. Waliwaua kwa upanga, wakauteketeza mji kwa moto.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo Wadani walichukua vitu ambavyo Mika alikuwa amevifanya, na kuhani aliyekuwa amemfanyia kazi. Kisha walikwenda Laishi, wakawashambulia watu wake, waliokuwa wametulia bila kutazamia taabu. Waliwaua kwa panga zao, wakauchoma mji moto.

decisions.choice: what Micah had made: the narrator names the gods as things made by a man
decisions.reason: Micah called them "my gods" (verse 24); the narrator calls them "what Micah had made", which stresses that they were made by human hands.

decisions.choice: a people quiet and secure: the narrator repeats their helplessness
decisions.reason: The words repeat the spies' report (verses 7, 10). Laish was a far-off, peaceful town, not one of the peoples Israel was told to drive out, and it had no defenders. The repetition keeps the people of Laish before the reader as the attack falls on them.

decisions.choice: with the mouth of the sword: with the edge of the sword, killing them
decisions.reason: The edge of a sword is called its "mouth", as if it devoured. The phrase means they killed the people (1:8, 25).

decisions.choice: struck them down with the sword; killed them with their swords
decisions.reason: As in 1:8: Literal keeps "the edge of the sword"; Balanced and Readable give the sense.

records.literal_gloss: And there [was] no deliverer, for far [was] it from Sidon, and a word there [was] not to them with man; and it [was] in the valley which [belongs] to Beth-rehob; and they rebuilt the city and dwelt in it.

en.L: And there was no one to deliver [them], for it [was] far from Sidon, and they had no dealings with anyone. And it [was] in the valley that [belongs] to Beth-rehob. And they rebuilt the city and lived in it.
en.B: There was no one to rescue them, because the city was far from Sidon and they had no dealings with anyone. It lay in the valley that belongs to Beth-rehob. The Danites rebuilt the city and settled there.
en.R: No one came to save them, because they lived far from Sidon and had nothing to do with anyone else. The town was in the valley near Beth-rehob. The Danites rebuilt the town and lived there.

sw.L: Wala hapakuwa na mwokozi, kwa maana [ulikuwa] mbali na Sidoni, wala hawakuwa na shughuli na mtu yeyote. Nao [ulikuwa] katika bonde lililo la Beth-rehobu. Nao wakaujenga mji upya, wakakaa ndani yake.
sw.B: Hapakuwa na mtu wa kuwaokoa, kwa sababu mji ulikuwa mbali na Sidoni, wala hawakuwa na shughuli na mtu yeyote. Ulikuwa katika bonde lililo la Beth-rehobu. Wadani waliujenga mji upya, wakakaa humo.
sw.R: Hakuna aliyekuja kuwaokoa, kwa sababu waliishi mbali na Sidoni, wala hawakuwa na uhusiano na mtu mwingine yeyote. Mji huo ulikuwa katika bonde karibu na Beth-rehobu. Wadani waliujenga mji upya, wakaishi humo.

decisions.choice: no one to deliver them: no ally came to their rescue
decisions.reason: This is what the spies noticed in verse 7: Laish was far from Sidon and had ties with no one, so no one came to its help.

decisions.choice: the valley that belongs to Beth-rehob: the valley at the head of the Jordan, toward Aram
decisions.reason: Beth-rehob, or Rehob, was a town to the north, later named among the Aramean peoples (Numbers 13:21; 2 Samuel 10:6). The valley is the upper Jordan valley, where Laish stood.

decisions.choice: with anyone: as in verse 7
alternatives: they had no dealings with Aram
decisions.reason: As in verse 7, some copies of the Greek translation read "Aram" in place of "man, anyone". The Hebrew reading is followed here.

decisions.choice: the Danites
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the Danites as the ones who rebuilt the city, so the subject does not seem to be the people of Laish.

source.text: וַיִּקְרְא֤וּ שֵׁם־הָעִיר֙ דָּ֔ן בְּשֵׁם֙ דָּ֣ן אֲבִיהֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר יוּלַּ֖ד לְיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְאוּלָ֛ם לַ֥יִשׁ שֵׁם־הָעִ֖יר לָרִאשֹׁנָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And they called [the] name of the city Dan, by [the] name of Dan their father who was born to Israel; but Laish [was the] name of the city at the first.

en.L: And they called the name of the city Dan, after the name of Dan their father, who was born to Israel; but Laish [was] the name of the city at first.
en.B: They named the city Dan, after their ancestor Dan, who was born to Israel; but the city used to be called Laish.
en.R: They named the town Dan, after their ancestor Dan, who was one of the sons of Israel. Before that, the town had been called Laish.

sw.L: Nao wakaliita jina la mji Dani, kwa jina la Dani baba yao, aliyezaliwa kwa Israeli; lakini jina la mji hapo kwanza [lilikuwa] Laishi.
sw.B: Waliuita mji huo Dani, kwa jina la babu yao Dani, aliyezaliwa kwa Israeli; lakini zamani mji huo uliitwa Laishi.
sw.R: Waliuita mji huo Dani, kwa jina la babu yao Dani, aliyekuwa mmoja wa wana wa Israeli. Kabla ya hapo, mji huo uliitwa Laishi.

decisions.choice: Dan their father, born to Israel: their ancestor, son of Jacob
decisions.reason: "Father" here means ancestor. Israel is Jacob, whose son Dan was born to him by Bilhah (Genesis 30:5-6).

decisions.choice: they named the city Dan: the town that marks the northern edge of Israel
decisions.reason: From now on Dan is the northern limit of the land, as in the phrase "from Dan to Beersheba" (20:1; 1 Samuel 3:20). Joshua 19:47 tells the same renaming.

decisions.choice: one of the sons of Israel
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly that Dan was one of Israel's sons.

records.literal_gloss: And set up for themselves [the] sons of Dan the carved image; and Jonathan son of Gershom son of Manasseh, he and his sons were priests to [the] tribe of the Danite[s] until [the] day of [the] exile of the land.

en.L: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Dan set up the carved image for themselves; and Jonathan son of Gershom, son of Manasseh, he and his sons were priests to the tribe of the Danites until the day the land went into exile.
en.B: The Danites set up the carved image for themselves. Jonathan son of Gershom, son of Manasseh, and his sons served as priests for the tribe of Dan until the time the land went into exile.
en.R: The Danites set up the carved idol for themselves. Jonathan, the son of Gershom, the son of Manasseh, served as priest for the tribe of Dan. He and his sons after him were priests for the tribe until the time the people of the land were taken away as captives.

sw.L: Nao wana wa Dani wakajisimamishia sanamu ya kuchonga; naye Yonathani mwana wa Gershomu, mwana wa Manase, yeye na wanawe walikuwa makuhani wa kabila la Wadani mpaka siku ile nchi ilipochukuliwa uhamishoni.
sw.B: Wadani walijisimamishia ile sanamu ya kuchonga. Yonathani mwana wa Gershomu, mwana wa Manase, pamoja na wanawe, walihudumu kama makuhani wa kabila la Dani mpaka wakati nchi ilipochukuliwa uhamishoni.
sw.R: Wadani walijisimamishia ile sanamu ya kuchonga. Yonathani, mwana wa Gershomu, mwana wa Manase, alihudumu kama kuhani wa kabila la Dani. Yeye na wanawe baada yake walikuwa makuhani wa kabila hilo mpaka wakati watu wa nchi hiyo walipochukuliwa mateka.

decisions.choice: Manasseh, as written; a raised letter shows the name was first Moses
decisions.reason: In the Hebrew manuscripts the name is written with its second letter, nun (n), raised above the line; the pinned source data writes it in line with the other letters. Without that letter, the same consonants spell "Moses". Gershom was the name of Moses' son (Exodus 2:22; 18:3), and Moses' family were Levites, as the young man of 17:7 was, while Manasseh was a tribe, not a priestly family. Some copies of the Greek translation and the Latin Vulgate read "Moses". Jewish tradition explains the raised letter as added out of respect for Moses, so that a descendant of his serving an image would not be named as his. The written name is kept here, and the raised letter itself points to "Moses" as the earlier reading.

decisions.choice: son of: son or later descendant
decisions.reason: "Son of" can mean a descendant some generations later. Jonathan may be a grandson of Moses (if that reading is followed) or a later member of the family; the Hebrew does not say which.

decisions.choice: Jonathan: probably the young Levite of chapters 17-18, named only now
decisions.reason: The young Levite has had no name until this point. Naming him here, at the end, with his family line, most likely tells the reader who the hired priest was. The Hebrew does not say so in so many words.

decisions.choice: until the exile of the land: probably the Assyrian deportations from the north
alternatives: the capture of the ark in Eli's time
decisions.reason: The phrase most likely refers to the time the Assyrians carried off the people of northern Israel, first from Galilee and the region of Dan (2 Kings 15:29), and then after the fall of Samaria (2 Kings 17:6). Some take "the land" to mean the time the ark was captured and Shiloh lost (1 Samuel 4:21-22; Psalm 78:60-61), which would fit verse 31.

decisions.choice: the sons of Dan set up the carved image: Dan remained a place of image worship
decisions.reason: Later Jeroboam set up one of his two golden calves at Dan (1 Kings 12:28-30). The shrine of Micah's image is the first chapter of that history.

decisions.choice: until the time the land went into exile; until the time the people of the land were taken away as captives
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "the day"; Balanced says "the time", since "day" here means a period. Readable says what exile was.

decisions.choice: "Yonathani mwana wa Gershomu, mwana wa Manase"
decisions.reason: The names follow the usual Swahili forms with a final vowel; "Manase" is written as the Hebrew text reads it, and the meaning decision (m1) explains the raised letter that points to Moses ("Musa").

records.literal_gloss: And they set up for themselves [the] carved image of Micah which he had made, all [the] days of [the] being [of the] house of God in Shiloh.

en.L: And they set up for themselves the carved image of Micah that he had made, all the days that the house of God was in Shiloh.
en.B: They kept Micah's carved image, which he had made, set up for themselves the whole time the house of God was at Shiloh.
en.R: The Danites kept Micah's carved idol set up for themselves the whole time that God's house was at Shiloh.

sw.L: Nao wakajisimamishia sanamu ya kuchonga ya Mika aliyoifanya, siku zote ambazo nyumba ya Mungu ilikuwa Shilo.
sw.B: Waliendelea kuwa na sanamu ya kuchonga ya Mika, aliyoifanya, ikiwa imesimamishwa kwa ajili yao muda wote ambao nyumba ya Mungu ilikuwa Shilo.
sw.R: Wadani waliendelea kuwa na sanamu ya kuchonga ya Mika ikiwa imesimamishwa kwa ajili yao muda wote ambao nyumba ya Mungu ilikuwa Shilo.

decisions.choice: the house of God in Shiloh: the tabernacle, Israel's place of worship
decisions.reason: The tabernacle stood at Shiloh from Joshua's time (Joshua 18:1) until the days of Eli and Samuel (1 Samuel 1:3, 24; 4:3-4; Jeremiah 7:12). The book ends this story by setting Micah's image at Dan beside the true house of God at Shiloh; Micah had called his own shrine a "house of God" too (17:5).

decisions.choice: they set up ... which he had made: the image stays in use for a long time
decisions.reason: The verse goes back over verse 30 and gives the length of time the image was kept: as long as the house of God stood at Shiloh. Calling it the image "Micah had made" repeats that it was the work of a man (verse 27).

decisions.choice: kept ... set up
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "kept ... set up", since the verse speaks of how long the image stayed in use.
